description: Solo participant tackling this challenge independently. Focused on data analysis, visualization, and building a creative data driven solution. Team is closed and not looking for new members
summary:
Project AeroData: The Earth Information Jukebox
AeroData transforms multi-source NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) telemetry and atmospheric data into an interactive, data-driven experience. Built with Python and modern visualization utilities, it empowers researchers, students, and space enthusiasts to explore planetary metrics dynamically, bridging complex aerospace datasets with intuitive, accessible visualization
details:
Project AeroData: The Earth Information Jukebox is an interactive web application built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 ("The Earth Information Jukebox" track)[span_2](start_span)[span_2](end_span)[span_3](start_span)[span_3](end_span). It transforms complex, multi-decade NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) climate and atmospheric datasets—including global CO2 concentrations, surface temperature anomalies, sea level rise, and Arctic sea ice extent—into an intuitive, multi-sensory exploration experience[span_4](start_span)[span_4](end_span)[span_5](start_span)[span_5](end_span).

How It Works:

Users can select curated planetary "tracks," scrub across historical timelines (1980–2026), compare two environmental variables side-by-side, and experience synchronized visual charts paired with data sonification (harmonic pitch mapping) and plain-language scientific narratives[span_6](start_span)[span_6](end_span).

Tools & Technologies Used:

Developed in Python using modular data ingestion (data/), statistical processing and anomaly scaling (utils/), and a clean browser-based dashboard (app.py)[span_7](start_span)[span_7](end_span)[span_8](start_span)[span_8](end_span).

Intended Impact & Creativity:

By turning raw scientific feeds into an accessible, jukebox-style interface, AeroData lowers the technical barrier to NASA Earth science for students, educators, and visually impaired learners—promoting global climate literacy and self-guided discovery[span_9](start_span)[span_9](end_span)
